title: Hosted API - embeddings + rerank demo (Gravitas Search)
summary: AE and SE walked Gravitas through Redwood hosted embeddings and reranking endpoints focusing on search relevance improvements, latency/cost tradeoffs, and security/compliance (VPC, KMS, SOC2). Agreed next steps: send pricing and security pack, run 1k query benchmark, schedule pilot kickoff week of 2026-10-26.
action_items: Maya Thompson: Send pricing sheet and Redwood hosted security pack (due 2026-10-20)
Ethan Park: Share sample rerank payloads and a simple benchmark script (due 2026-10-21)
Priya Nair / Gravitas: Provide 1k anonymized queries + ground-truth relevance for benchmark (due 2026-10-22)
Sam Ruiz: Confirm pilot stakeholders and go/no-go criteria (due 2026-10-23)
next_steps: Redwood to send pricing and security docs
Customer to share query sample and success criteria
Schedule pilot kickoff (30-45 minute tech sync) for week of 2026-10-26
SE to run baseline 1k-query rerank benchmark and share results
transcript:
Meeting header: Date/Time: 2026-10-19 15:00 UTC | Duration approx 62m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Lina (Redwood Product), Oliver (Gravitas Head of Search), Priya (Gravitas SRE), Sam (Gravitas PM), Talia (Gravitas DS)

00:00 - Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick intro - I'm Maya, AE on the Redwood team, with Ethan our SE. Today we'll show the hosted embeddings + rerank flow and how teams typically wire it into search relevance.
00:14 - Oliver: Hey thanks, we've been excited to see this. High level our goal is to improve search relevance across web + docs, reduce apparent latency, and not blow the infra budget.
00:24 - Maya: Great, that's exactly what we'll target. Quick qual - can you remind us what your current stack is?
00:30 - Sam: We're running OpenSearch for indexing, a vector store backed by Elastic's dense vector plugin, and some homegrown reranker that hits a BERT model on a small GPU cluster. Latency is okay for batch, but p99 is bad during peaks.
00:45 - Ethan: Cool. Do you store embeddings in the index or call on the fly?
00:48 - Talia: We're storing precomputed embeddings. We tried on-the-fly for cold queries but it was slow and expensive.
00:55 - Ethan: Makes sense. For the demo we'll show both approaches: precomputed + hosted embeddings for vector search, and the rerank endpoint which gets top-K from your index then recomputes relevance scores using the rerank model.
01:05 - Priya: Security question up front, do you support VPC peering or private endpoints? We can't send PII out of our VPC for the pilot.
01:12 - Maya: Yes - Redwood hosted supports private networking options (VPC endpoints), and our Private product is available for full air-gapped deployments. For hosted we can do customer-managed VPC peering and KMS integrations for key management. We'll send the security pack after the call.
01:25 - Oliver: And compliance - SOC2 / audit logs?
01:27 - Lina: We are SOC2 compliant; audit logs and request-level trace IDs are available through the Console and can be exported. We'll include the SOC2 attestation in the docs.

01:40 - Demo start: Ethan shared his screen.
01:43 - Ethan: Alright, walkthrough: first the embeddings endpoint. Here's a simple POST to /v1/embeddings with payload text. We return a 1536-d vector by default (model: rdx-embed-1536). Small note - model family names sometimes get transcribed wrong by tools as 'redbox' or 'rdx' in our docs, it's r-d-x embed.
02:05 - Sam: Wait, 1536 dims - will that fit our index? We currently use 512 dims for speed.
02:10 - Ethan: You can choose smaller models or project down - Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization or smaller dims based on recall thresholds. For demo I'll show 1536 then a 512 projection path.
02:20 - Ethan: Next - the rerank endpoint: you call /v1/rerank with a candidate list (top 50 from OpenSearch) plus original query. The endpoint returns a score and optionally a delta explanation.
02:34 - Talia: Is rerank running on the same model as embeddings?
02:36 - Ethan: Not necessarily. The reranker is a cross-encoder style model that looks at query + doc pair. It can run on an optimized variant for lower latency. We have both dense-sparse hybrid suggestions and a lightweight cross-encoder for p50 speed.
02:50 - Oliver: Latency numbers? p50/p95?
02:52 - Ethan: For hosted: embeddings vector retrieval is sub-10ms for nns with a vector DB, rerank cross-encoder p50 around 60-120ms depending on model size and sequence length; p95 could be 300-600ms if you exceed KV cache or hit cold starts. We'll demo caching and batching improvements.
03:12 - Priya: Sounds reasonable. What's the cost delta if we run rerank for top 10 vs top 50?
03:18 - Ethan: Rough rule: cost roughly scales with number of pairs scored. If cross-encoder costs X per pair, 50x vs 10x. Redwood Optimize can suggest doing small candidate sets plus a cheap prefilter to reduce pairs, or using distinction thresholds so you only rerank when initial score ambiguity is high.
03:35 - Ethan: I'll show an example pipeline in the Console: route A calls embeddings for query, gets top-100 from your OpenSearch, then a filter step (fast lexical re-rank), then we call hosted /v1/rerank on top-20.
03:50 - Screen shows Console route config, caching toggle, and batching slider.
04:00 - Ethan: There's a batching knob - continuous batching pools similar requests for a short window. Helps throughput without impacting p50 too much. Also prefix KV cache: if user frequently asks for certain query prefixes, KV cache keeps decoder state so subsequent tokens are faster.
04:16 - Sam: For search, most queries are short but we do a lot of faceted queries, slightly different tokens. How effective is prefix cache?
04:22 - Ethan: Varies - it's best for autocomplete. For rerank you get KV cache benefits across hot doc evaluation when doc sequences are repeated. We'll run a benchmark to show expected savings.

04:45 - Demo: live run with sample dataset. Ethan sends a request flow: query -> embeddings -> topK -> rerank.
04:50 - Voice overlaps / brief network blip.
04:55 - Ethan: Here's a sample payload (sloppy transcription): {query: "enterprise search best practices", candidates: [{id: 123, text: "..."}, ...]} and the reranker returns scores and a small explanation snippet. The console also shows token-level cost and latency breakdown.
05:18 - Priya: The explanation looks useful. Is that deterministic?
05:21 - Ethan: It's model-dependent and we can control randomness (temperature) to make scores stable. For rerank we usually run deterministic inference (temp 0) so scores are repeatable.
05:29 - Talia: Any gotchas with embeddings drift or model upgrades? We have concerns about quality regressions when models are upgraded.
05:35 - Lina: We have version pinning and rollout controls - you can pin model versions for traffic and use canary rollouts. Redwood Optimize also tracks eval sets and alerts on regressions. We'll show a quick eval dashboard.
05:48 - Screen: Optimize eval dashboard with regression alert example.
06:05 - Oliver: Great. On to architecture questions: if we go hosted, do you support private customer data retention policies? We need logs for 90 days, but not raw user text retained in plaintext for longer than 7 days.
06:18 - Maya: We support retention policy controls per workspace; logs and traces can be kept as you require and PII scrubbing is available. For customers with stricter needs we recommend Redwood Private. We'll include details in the security pack.
06:32 - Sam: Do you store embeddings derived from customer data?
06:35 - Lina: By default hosted store embeddings encrypted at rest; you can opt-in to delete policies or customer-managed keys. We'll document options.

06:50 - Benchmarks discussion: Ethan runs quick benchmark with Gravitas sample (sanitized).
07:00 - Ethan: Running a 1k-query baseline: step 1 is raw OpenSearch topK recall; step 2 is after hosted rerank. Looking at MRR and relevance uplift.
07:12 - Talia: For quality metrics we want MRR@10, nDCG and a manual inspection of failure cases.
07:18 - Ethan: Yep -- we'll produce the full results and suggest an A/B test for your UI to measure engagement.

15:45 - (middle of call) Discussion on edge cases, costs and fallback strategies
15:50 - Oliver: If the hosted reranker latency spikes, can we fall back to local BERT?
15:55 - Ethan: Yes - Redwood supports policy routing. You can specify a fallback to a smaller hosted variant or your on-prem model. There's automatic fallback on errors or SLA violations.
16:08 - Priya: How does the billing look for bursty traffic? We have weekly batch jobs and unpredictable user peaks.
16:15 - Maya: For Hosted we bill per request/token; for sustained bursts you can add Reserved capacity (Dedicated) or configure burst queues. We can show cost projections after we see your traffic profile.

22:30 - Security deep dive (short)
22:33 - Priya: KMS integration examples - do you support AWS KMS or GCP KMS?
22:36 - Lina: We support AWS KMS and GCP KMS for hosted and the Private option can use HSM. We'll attach docs.

30:10 - Pilot planning
30:12 - Maya: For pilot we recommend 1) share 1k anonymized queries + ground-truth 2) Redwood runs baseline rerank vs your current rerank 3) We'll do a 2-week pilot with weekly checkins and a tech sync to review results.
30:28 - Sam: That timeline works; our stakeholders want results before end of month.
30:33 - Maya: Ok we'll aim to start the pilot week of Oct 26.

49:40 - Closing Qs and recap
49:42 - Oliver: Quick question, can rerank output be used to update index ranking features? We want to feed signals back into OpenSearch.
49:50 - Ethan: Yes, you can use the rerank scores as additional fields or signals and reindex periodically. Also you can use online features to store a precomputed 'final_score' on write.
49:58 - Talia: Any gotchas with rate limiting? If we plan to send bulk candidate batches during reindexing, will we hit API limits?
50:06 - Maya: We have rate limits by default but for pilots we can temporarily raise limits and discuss a committed throughput for Dedicated. We'll include suggested rate limits in the doc.
50:25 - Maya: Alright quick recap of next steps: we'll send pricing & security docs, Ethan will share sample payloads and benchmark script, Gravitas to share 1k queries and success criteria. Pilot kickoff week of Oct 26.
50:40 - Oliver: Sounds good. Thanks, this was helpful.
50:44 - Maya: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with an email with the attachments and calendar invites for the pilot kickoff.
50:53 - (call ends)

Note: transcript contains mild transcription artifacts (model names sometimes mis-typed e.g., 'rdx' vs 'redwood', some punctuation missing).
